body_markdown:
On


[The Toast](https://open.spotify.com/show/2pC9RlB48sW1pwtz5PieJE?si=aa556b434aa64027) *,* their daily pop culture and news podcast, sisters


**Jackie** and


**Claudia Oshry** have spent nearly a decade turning the stories everyone is talking about into can’t-miss morning conversations. Five days a week, the duo deliver their takes on the day’s biggest headlines, keeping “Toasters” coming back with laughs, insider lingo, and major sisterly side-eye.


Now,


*The Toast* has landed a spot on the official list of 30 podcasts eligible for Best Podcast at the 84th Golden Globe Awards. The category is returning for its second year, reflecting podcasts’ growing place in the entertainment landscape.


*For the Record* caught up with Jackie and Claudia about keeping up with the pop culture cycle, why video has always been part of


*The Toast* experience, and what it means to see the medium recognized on the big stage.


### **For someone discovering** ***The Toast*** **for the first time, how would you describe it?**


**Claudia:** The feedback we get most often is that our show feels like a group chat with your best friends catching up every morning. I think that’s always been the case because we’re sisters, and our dynamic is one that a lot of people can relate to.


It’s also a really approachable format. You don’t need to have listened to last week’s episodes to know what’s going on. You can tune in every morning, pop in and out, or binge whenever you want, and we’ll be here.


### **The show’s Fast Five is a daily rundown of the biggest stories in pop culture. How do you decide what makes the cut?**


**Jackie:** Every morning I probably have 10 to 12 of the biggest stories from the last 24 hours to sort through before narrowing them down. Some stories deserve a dedicated segment, while others might just get a passing mention in our pre-Fast Five banter.


It’s not always about what’s making the biggest headlines, but what we think will make for the most interesting discussion. We can go from laughing about something completely ridiculous to having a more serious, nuanced conversation about a much bigger issue, sometimes within the same episode.


### **You release five episodes a week, plus occasional bonus episodes. How do you keep up with a fast-moving news cycle while bringing fresh energy to the mic each day?**


**Claudia:** First of all, thank you for noticing how hard we work! We’ve been a daily podcast for so many years now, and I truly think that’s one of the things that sets us apart.


**Jackie:** As for the energy, I really think being sisters is what keeps things fun every day. We actually try to hold off on talking about the news with each other until we record so we can have those conversations in real time. We’re not exaggerating when we say we’re genuinely excited to see each other every morning, catch up, gossip, and laugh.


### **You’ve been using video long before it became an expected part of the format. What has the visual element added for your fans?**


**Claudia:** We started our podcast nine years ago, and video was important to us from the get-go. I think if you ask any Toaster, they’ll say there’s a big difference between listening to an episode and watching it. So much of our dynamic comes through in our body language, the facial expressions, and moments you just can’t really capture through audio.


### **What does it mean to you to have the medium recognized at the Golden Globes?**


**Claudia:** It’s huge. We’ve always thought of


*The Toast* as a modern morning show. Our listeners tune in every day to get their news, hear our takes, and feel like they’re part of a larger conversation. So it feels appropriate that podcasting is finally being taken seriously alongside other forms of entertainment. We knew nine years ago that podcasting was going to be big, and it’s exciting to see it finally getting its flowers.
